originalTitle: SK Hynix's $28 billion US IPO to test its $1 trillion AI rally. Here's how
simplifiedContent: SK Hynix, a company that makes computer chips, is trying to raise about $28 billion by selling shares on the US stock market. This is a big test to see if investors are still excited about companies that are involved in artificial intelligence (AI). The money raised will be used to expand SK Hynix's semiconductor business. This is important because it will show if investors are still willing to invest in companies that make AI-related products, which have been very popular lately. If the sale is successful, it could be a good sign for other similar companies.

originalTitle: AI investors may pivot to hyperscalers from chipmakers, Morgan Stanley says
simplifiedContent: Morgan Stanley, a big investment company, is suggesting that investors should change their focus from companies that make computer chips to bigger companies that use artificial intelligence, like Alphabet (the company that owns Google) and Amazon. This is because they think interest rates might not go up as much as expected, and oil prices might go down, which would help certain types of companies. As a result, investors might start to move their money away from chip-making companies, which could cause their stocks to go down. This shift in investment strategy could be significant for the stock market and the companies involved. Morgan Stanley's recommendation is based on the idea that big companies are investing heavily in AI, and investors are looking for results.

originalTitle: Trump rings Wall Street's opening bells as he ties his presidency to stock market gains
simplifiedContent: President Trump recently opened the stock market from his office, which is a symbolic gesture. He is trying to connect his presidency to the stock market doing well, but many people are worried about inflation, which is when prices for things like food and housing go up. Only about a third of people think he's doing a good job with the economy. Trump also announced "Trump Accounts" to help kids start investing in the stock market, which could be helpful because many families don't have money invested in the stock market. This is important because it shows that Trump is trying to take credit for the stock market's performance, but not everyone is happy with his economic leadership.

originalTitle: Rentomojo gets SEBI nod for raising funds through IPO launch. Details here
simplifiedContent: Rentomojo, a company that rents out furniture, has gotten approval from the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) to raise money by selling stocks to the public. This is called an Initial Public Offering (IPO). The company wants to raise up to ₹150 crore, which it will use to expand its business and pay off debts. Existing shareholders will be selling some of their stocks as part of this IPO. This is important because it shows that Rentomojo is a significant player in the online rental market in India and is now looking to grow further.

originalTitle: Q1FY27 IT earnings preview: Brokerages see mixed quarter as AI, macro headwinds weigh on growth
simplifiedContent: The earnings season for tech companies is about to start, and experts have low expectations due to economic uncertainty and changes caused by artificial intelligence (AI). This means they think the companies might not have done as well as they could have from April to June. Analysts are worried that global tensions and AI are affecting the companies' performance, and they want to see the companies' future plans and predictions for demand. They expect the growth of these companies to be slower than before. This is important because it can affect the companies' stock prices and the overall stock market.

originalTitle: Wall Street edges higher as chip stocks rebound
simplifiedContent: The stock market is doing a little better today, with some important groups of stocks, like those related to computer chips, bouncing back. This has helped the three main measures of the market: the S&P 500, the Nasdaq Composite, and the Dow Jones Industrial Average, to go up a bit. The S&P 500 is up 0.4%, the Nasdaq Composite is up 0.8%, and the Dow Jones Industrial Average is up 0.2%. This matters because it shows that investors are feeling a bit more positive about the market. As of 9:35 a.m. Eastern Time, these small gains are a good sign for the market, but it's still early in the day.
